### The Phantom of the River: The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle

The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*), also known as Cantor’s giant softshell turtle, is one of the world's most unique and elusive freshwater reptiles. Found in slow-moving rivers and estuaries across Southeast Asia, this species is more of an ambush predator than a typical turtle. It spends an estimated 95% of its life buried motionless in sand or mud at the bottom of a river, with only its eyes and snout protruding. This "frog-faced" turtle surfaces just twice a day to take a breath before disappearing again beneath the sediment.

![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Pelochelys_cantorii_fg.jpg/1280px-Pelochelys_cantorii_fg.jpg)
*The distinctive face of the Asian Giant Softshell Turtle. Photo: F. Wicker.*

Instead of a hard, bony shell, the Asian Giant Softshell has a smooth, leathery, and olive-colored carapace that feels like rubber. This flat, aerodynamic body allows it to bury itself efficiently. Growing to over three feet in length, it is a formidable predator, using its powerful jaws to snatch unsuspecting fish, crustaceans, and mollusks that swim too close.

Unfortunately, this remarkable creature is facing a silent crisis. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) lists the Asian Giant Softshell Turtle as Critically Endangered. Its survival is severely threatened by habitat destruction from dam construction, sand mining, and pollution. Furthermore, it is illegally harvested throughout its range for its meat and eggs, which are considered a delicacy in many regions. Conservation organizations like the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) are working to protect its nesting sites and raise hatchlings in captivity for release, offering a glimmer of hope for this phantom of the river.

![](https://inaturalist-open-data.s3.amazonaws.com/photos/1014352/large.jpeg)
*The full body of an Asian Giant Softshell Turtle, showing its leathery carapace. Photo: K. S. Seshadri.*

***

### Bibliography

Asian Turtle Trade Working Group. “Pelochelys cantorii.” *The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species*, 2000, www.iucnredlist.org/species/16502/97398634.

Bittel, Jason. “‘Extinct’ Giant Turtle Found, Melts Hearts.” *National Geographic*, 19 May 2015, www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/article/150519-cantors-giant-softshell-turtle-india-animals-conservation-science.

“Cantor's Giant Softshell Turtle.” *Wildlife Conservation Society*, www.wcs.org/our-work/species/cantors-giant-softshell-turtle. Accessed 26 May 2024.
